transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-09
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Connor (Redwood SE), Maya (KiteBank - Head of ML), Rajiv (Eng Manager), Sophie (InfoSec), Leo (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
- Primary objective: scope POC for KiteBank to validate that Redwood's runtime can meet privacy and retention requirements while keeping prompt storage optional; agree on benchmarks, sample data, and timeline.
- Key concerns: PII in prompts, encryption & KMS, retention windows, prompt storage vs ephemeral-only logging, redaction accuracy, SOC2 artifacts and VPC connectivity.
- Agreed next steps: Redwood to send SOW/Security checklist; customer to provide sample prompts and traffic patterns; schedule SE benchmarking session.

Topics: POC success criteria; workload sizing and expected QPS; benchmark metrics (95p latency, tokens/sec); logging/redaction approach; prompt storage options (never store / hashed store / opt-in); retention config; security artifacts and network connectivity.

Transcript:
00:00 Aisha (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, I think we've got about 50 minutes, right? This is the privacy and prompt storage piece for the KiteBank proof of concept. Connor's our SE and will walk through the benchmark ask and retention options.
00:18 Maya (KiteBank): Yep, thanks. Quick note, Sophie from InfoSec will jump in on the security items. We're mainly trying to nail down whether we can run with ephemeral prompts in the hosted API or whether we need private deployment. Latency is important too.
00:30 Connor (Redwood SE): Great, quick agenda — success criteria, workload sizing (qps/seq lengths), benchmark plan, and then data handling: redaction/retention/prompt storage. Also sharing links — I'll drop the benchmark spreadsheet after.
00:45 Rajiv (KiteBank): For context, our typical flow is a 2-turn conversational flow for support chat and a separate document summarization pipeline. Live chat peaks ~120 qps but average is 22 qps; doc summary jobs are batch overnight, heavier token counts.
01:05 Sophie (KiteBank, InfoSec): Our compliance ask is strict: PII should not be retained beyond 30 days unless encrypted and logged with audit trail. We also want to avoid storing raw prompts by default.
01:20 Aisha: Ok that clarifies. Two paths: 1) Hosted API with prompt redaction and optional hashed prompt storage; 2) Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) where prompts never leave your network. Both can meet latency, but tradeoffs are in ops and cost.
01:34 Maya: Can you clarify 'hashed prompt storage' — what does that mean? Is it reversible?
01:40 Connor: Good question. Hashed means we store a digest for dedup/cache or replay correlation; it's one-way (SHA-like) and not reversible. We also record minimal metadata — model, route, token counts, timestamp. Full prompt is not retained unless you opt in. Note: if you need redaction, we recommend both regexes and ML-based PII detectors. Regex alone misses many cases.
02:05 Sophie: ML detectors sound good but we need to know false-positive / false-negative rates. Does Redwood provide any metrics?
02:12 Connor: We have internal evals on common PII types — emails, credit card patterns, national ids — and the detector tuned for recall at ~95% for structured patterns. For free-text, you should expect recall to drop; that's why we recommend a hybrid: regex for structured items plus ML for free-form. I'll attach the detector tuning notes.
02:38 Leo (Product): For the POC success criteria, can we list the measurable things? E.g., 95th pct latency < 250ms, 99th < 600ms, cost per 1M tokens < $X, and redaction false negative rate < 1%?
02:52 Aisha: Yes, let's put that in the SOW. For latency numbers we need exact target per workload (chat vs batch). Connor, can you map model variants to expected latencies on our hosted vs dedicated configs?
03:06 Connor: Sure — rough numbers: on Redwood Hosted with quantized Llama2-13B variant we expect 95p latency ~180–220ms for chat with 8-token responses and KV cache hit rates; on Dedicated with pinned GPUs you can see slightly lower variance, maybe 160–200ms. For batch doc summaries (long context), throughput measured in tokens/sec matters more; that's more GPU-bound. I'll include a small table in the benchmark plan. Note: those numbers assume continuous batching turned on; cold-starts are higher.
03:38 Rajiv: What about prompt storage during batching? If we do prefix caching, does that store prompts? We can't have raw PII in cache.
03:46 Connor: Prefix/KV cache is per-request runtime memory — we don't persist raw input to long term stores unless logging is enabled. For POC you can set runtime to ephemeral-only — no logs persisted. But that affects our ability to run some analytics and regression tests.
04:02 Sophie: So ephemeral-only means no post-hoc debugging. Is there a middle ground?
04:08 Aisha: Middle ground is storing redacted prompts — strip PII before persisting — plus hashed digests for correlating requests. We can show a config that redacts at ingestion via our redaction pipeline.
04:18 Maya: Do you support streaming redaction — like redact before it hits logs?
04:22 Connor: Yes, we support pre-ingest redaction hooks. There's a short pipeline: 1) pre-ingest filter (regex + ML), 2) optional redact/replace tokens, 3) store redacted text or hashed digest only. This can run in your VPC or in our hosted flow depending on setup. If you require the PII never leave your VPC, Private deployment is the path.
04:45 Sophie: What encryption is used for stored prompts? KMS? HSM?
04:48 Connor: We integrate with AWS KMS/GCP KMS/Azure Key Vault; for Private we can support HSM-backed keys. All at-rest artifacts are AES-256 encrypted and access logged. We'll include SOC2 artifacts in the security checklist.
05:05 Maya: Nice. About retention windows — we might need 30 days for most, but regulatory holds could require 7 years for some records. Can Redwood tag and apply different retention rules?
05:18 Aisha: Yes, retention is configurable per-route or per-tenant. You can set TTLs: immediate deletion, 30d, 90d, 7y. Also support retention holds that block deletion until cleared. We'll include config examples.
05:33 Rajiv: For the POC we want to test: (a) ephemeral-only chat for 30k daily messages, (b) a hashed-prompt flow for dedup/cache for the same, (c) batch summarization with redaction. Can you size capacity for those?
05:46 Connor: Based on numbers: 30k messages/day average 0.35 qps sustained, peak 120 qps — we should test with a synthetic peak load: 150 qps sustained for 2 minutes to observe latency tail. For batch summarization, we need to run a 2-hour overnight job at scaled concurrency; I'll capture GPU-seconds estimate in the benchmark plan.
06:05 Sophie: Regarding logs for compliance — we need immutable audit logs for model version, who accessed keys, and redaction actions. Is that available?
06:12 Connor: Yes, audit logs for control plane actions and KMS key usage are available; we'll provide log retention options and sample log schema.
06:22 Maya: On the sample data we will share, it will contain PII. Can you accept a hashed or tokenized sample?
06:28 Aisha: You can do either: preferred to provide anonymized replicas — but we can accept hashed tokens. For the benchmark we need representative token lengths and the distribution. If you can provide clickstream with masked emails (like ****@example.com) that works too.
06:44 Leo: Timeline — what is a realistic POC duration? 4 weeks?
06:48 Aisha: Typical POCs are 3–6 weeks. For this scope I'd recommend 4 weeks: week 1 onboarding, week 2 benchmarking, week 3 functional validation (redaction config), week 4 wrap & findings. That aligns with your internal calendar?
06:59 Maya: Sounds good. We want to time a check-in with InfoSec after week 2 when you have the benchmark numbers.
07:06 Sophie: Yes I'll join. For acceptance criteria — we need: (1) no raw prompt retention by default, (2) redaction FN rate < 1% on our validation set, (3) latency SLOs per the table, (4) audit logs present and accessible.
07:20 Connor: Noted. We'll put those in the SOW as measurable pass/fail gates. For redaction FN measurement we'll run with your sample set and compute recall/precision. FYI — edge cases like pasted PDFs with OCR errors are tougher.
07:34 Rajiv: On network connectivity — we need VPC peering or a PrivateLink option. Do you support both?
07:39 Connor: We support VPC endpoints, PrivateLink (for AWS), and an on-prem package for air-gapped setups. For the POC, VPC endpoint + mTLS is usually fastest to stand up. We'll include a network checklist.
07:52 Maya: One more — do you persist prompts in any debug snapshots? I've seen other vendors capture responses for troubleshooting automatically. We can't allow that.
07:59 Aisha: We default to not persisting raw inputs. Debug snapshots are opt-in and require an explicit flag; we can make sure the POC environment disables snapshots by default. We'll also show how to create ephemeral-only routes.
08:14 Sophie: Can we get a contract addendum that says Redwood won't use our prompts for model training?
08:18 Aisha: Yes — we have a data-use clause; hosted customers can opt out of any model-training usage. We'll include the wording in the SOW; legal can follow up.
08:28 Leo: About the benchmark: can you test both your quantized and int8 variants? We want to see cost/latency tradeoffs.
08:33 Connor: Absolutely — we'll run the quantized 13B and a int8-optimized 13B-ish variant, plus a smaller 7B for cost comparisons. The benchmark spreadsheet will capture tokens/sec, cost per million tokens, and GPU-hours.
08:48 Rajiv: How do we measure cost for Dedicated vs Hosted?
08:51 Aisha: For Hosted we'll show a per-token estimate. For Dedicated we'll estimate GPU-hour costs amortized across throughput and include reserved pricing assumptions. We'll make the math explicit.
09:02 Maya: Regarding PII detection tuning — can we bring our in-house regex rules and feed them into the pre-ingest filter?
09:08 Connor: Yes, you can supply a rule set for regex-based redaction. We can also run your rules in a sandbox endpoint before the POC to measure coverage.
09:18 Sophie: On retention holds, we need an audit trail showing who placed or removed holds.
09:22 Connor: That's included in the audit schema — actions are user-tagged and timestamped. We also provide exportable CSVs for compliance.
09:32 Aisha: Ok, I'll recap the deliverables before we close. Redwood will: 1) send SOW and security checklist with SOC2 artifacts and data-use clause by Friday (2025-07-11); 2) Connor will send benchmark plan and spreadsheet with variant matrix by Sunday (2025-07-13); 3) we'll schedule an SE-led benchmark run w/ KiteBank team in week of 2025-07-21; 4) InfoSec will get a sandbox for redaction testing.
09:58 Maya: That covers it. Any blockers on Redwood side for receiving hashed/anonymized sample data?
10:03 Connor: No blockers, just a secure S3 or Data Transfer link and note about what is masked vs real. We'll provide an upload endpoint and the schema we expect.
10:12 Sophie: One last quick Q — do you have examples of retention config as IaC? We like terraform examples.
10:17 Aisha: Yes, we have a small terraform module for retention policies and redaction pipelines — we'll include a snippet in the SOW.
10:25 Leo: Great. If we get acceptable benchmark numbers and redaction results, next step is a pilot for 3 months.
10:30 Aisha: Sounds good. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
10:33 Meeting ended.
